decision: Statistics Canada table 14-10-0287-01 (monthly, seasonally adjusted) is the authoritative source for Canada's federal unemployment rate. The civic-voice-engine remains the ongoing scheduled owner of the document.

why_the_stored_value_is_stale: 1. The card's document, CA_unemploymentRate, is written ONLY by manual pipelines (canonical / live). Nothing schedules them. The stored document dates from a manual run on 2026-03-23.

2. The scheduled monthly job did fetch Canada unemployment, but under the stat name "unemployment", so it wrote CA_unemployment — a different document that the card never reads. Even a perfectly healthy monthly schedule could never refresh the card's document. (US and UK use "unemploymentRate" and are refreshed; Australia uses "unemployment" like Canada did.)
engine_investigation.why_the_stored_value_is_also_wrong: Table 14-10-0017-01 is "Labour force characteristics by gender and detailed age group, monthly, UNADJUSTED for seasonality" (confirmed from StatCan's cube metadata). For Canada / Unemployment rate / Total - Gender / 15 years and over, February 2026 it reports exactly 6.9 — the stored value. The engine labelled it "3-month moving average, seasonally adjusted". The unadjusted series is noisy (2026: Jun 6.1, Jul 6.7, Aug 7.3, Sep 6.2) whereas the verified seasonally adjusted series (14-10-0287-01) reads Feb 6.7 ... Sep 6.5.
engine_investigation.replace_or_merge: Targeted and canonical writers REPLACE the document (set without merge); canonical additionally wipes the whole collection first; the live and legacy writers merge. The app's one-off script merges.
other_findings_not_changed: Australia's scheduled job also uses the stat name "unemployment" (the same card-key mismatch). Out of scope (Australia untouched).
The canonical comment says 8 stats x 4 countries = 32 documents; the code defines 10 x 4 = 40.
The canonical upload's collection wipe is a standing hazard for ALL social_stats documents; unchanged (pre-flight added only for Canada unemployment).

ownership_solution.principle: One module defines the series, the verification, the document shape and the stat/document name, and every engine path that can write the card's document uses it.
engine: NEW src/ingestion/caUnemploymentMonthly.js: table 14-10-0287-01, coordinate 1.7.1.1.1.1.0.0.0.0, WDS API (axios -> fetch -> curl fallbacks), series identity verified against StatCan cube metadata BEFORE any value is trusted; pure document builder identical to the app's.

Scheduled targeted job fetchCA_Unemployment now returns stat "unemploymentRate" via that module, so the 1st-of-month schedule refreshes CA_unemploymentRate (the document the card reads). It no longer writes CA_unemployment.

live:fetch (fetchCALFS) uses the same module; canonical / live / targeted uploaders write the identical document for records carrying docOverride. Every record without docOverride is built exactly as before.
Canonical definition for Canada unemployment now carries the 14-10-0287-01 source and URL; the other 39 definitions are unchanged.
Pre-flight (before any wipe): a stale saved live_fetch file that still holds the old unadjusted value is refused so it can never be stored under the new label.
app: Overwrite guard: the script refuses to touch an existing document unless --approve-overwrite=<fingerprint> is supplied. The fingerprint identifies that exact stored state, is printed by the refusal, and stops matching if the document changes. It is NOT a boolean flag.
The target is read directly as well as queried, so an existing document that lacks the matching fields is still found.
A duplicate country/statName document under another id is refused with NO override; --allow-duplicate-stat was removed and now fails loudly.
merge:true preserves fields the script does not define; the script never deletes.
ownership_solution.consistency: Both repos' tests compare the two implementations when the sibling repo is present: identical constants, series members, and byte-identical documents from the same data. A live run against StatCan produced identical documents (6.5%, Sep 2026).

engine_ready_for_future_monthly_updates.detail: Once reviewed and deployed, the existing monthly cycle (1st of each month, 05:00) will fetch the verified seasonally adjusted series and write CA_unemploymentRate in the same shape the app script produces. Nothing has been deployed, pushed or activated, and the Firestore document has not been changed.
caveats: The first scheduled write will REPLACE the existing document (the targeted uploader uses set()). That is the intended handover, but it is a write to a document currently holding the engine's old unadjusted figure.
Whether the scheduler process is running anywhere is not knowable from the repository.

StatCan publishes the Labour Force Survey partway through the month (September 2026 data was released on 2026-10-09), but the cron fires on the 1st, so the card shows the PREVIOUS month until the following cycle. A later-in-month schedule would shorten that lag; not changed.
The old CA_unemployment document (if it exists) is orphaned and stale; not deleted.
